newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Bank of Taiwan cuts prime lending rate.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Taiwan cuts prime lending rate.

text.p: The Bank of Taiwan, the island's biggest commercial bank, said on Thursday it was cutting its prime lending rate to 7.025 percent from 7.05 percent, effective on Friday.
The state-owned bank, in a statement, said the reduction was adopted to comply with the government's policy of stimulating Taiwan's economy.

The announcement came less than an hour after Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong called on government agencies to join in a concerted effort to stimulate the flagging economy, saying the central bank could not achieve this alone.
Sheu did not specifically call for reductions in lending rates.
The Bank of Taiwan said it also was lowering rates for some time and savings deposits by 0.15 to 0.25 percentage points, also effective from Friday.
